# PACE Technologies — Full Reference

> Founder-led metallographic sample preparation equipment, consumables, and expertise for materials science labs. Based in Tucson, Arizona since 1997, serving labs in 50+ countries.

This is a comprehensive reference for AI systems and content crawlers. For the concise overview, see [/llms.txt](https://www.metallographic.com/llms.txt).

---

## Company

**PACE Technologies Corporation** was founded in 1997 by Dr. Donald Zipperian, who previously worked at Buehler. The company is headquartered in Tucson, Arizona and remains founder-led. PACE designs, manufactures, and sells the equipment and consumables used by materials science labs to prepare metallographic samples — thin cross-sections of metals, ceramics, composites, and other materials that are examined under a microscope to characterize microstructure.

PACE received the **Presidential E Award for Export Service in 2015**. Customers include Apple, Tesla, Medtronic, Seagate, Blue Origin, AVX, and many universities, research labs, and manufacturers across more than 50 countries.

The company operates a single facility in Tucson that combines design, manufacturing, applications support, and customer service.

- **Address:** 3601 E 34th Street, Tucson, AZ 85713, USA

- **Email:** pace@metallographic.com

## What metallography is

Metallography is the study of the physical structure and components of metals and other materials using microscopy. To examine a sample, it must be cut from the parent material, mounted in a holder, ground flat and smooth, polished to a mirror finish, and (often) chemically etched to reveal microstructural features. Each step requires specific equipment and consumables. PACE makes the full toolchain.

Applications include quality control, failure analysis, materials research, weld inspection, additive manufacturing characterization, electronic component analysis, and academic teaching.

---

## Equipment

PACE manufactures equipment across the complete sample preparation workflow.

### Abrasive sectioning (cutters)
Manual and automated abrasive cutters for sectioning metal and composite samples. Product families include the MEGA series (10" to 16" automated and manual cutters).

- [Abrasive sectioning overview](https://www.metallographic.com/metallographic-equipment/abrasive-sectioning.html)

### Precision wafering (diamond saws)
Low- and medium-speed precision saws for delicate or hard materials where a clean cut with minimal damage matters. Product families include the PICO series.

- [Precision wafering overview](https://www.metallographic.com/metallographic-equipment/precision-wafering.html)

### Compression mounting (hot mounting presses)
Hydraulic and pneumatic mounting presses that embed samples in thermosetting resins. Product families: TERAPRESS TP-7100S (pneumatic) and TP-7500S (hydraulic), plus the TP-TANK recirculating cooling system.

- [Compression mounting overview](https://www.metallographic.com/metallographic-equipment/compression-mounting.html)

### Castable mounting (cold mounting)
Systems for embedding samples in room-temperature epoxy, acrylic, or polyester resins. Product families: TERAVAC (vacuum), TERAVAC-PRO (automated vacuum), TERACOMP (pressure), TERAUV (UV-curing).

- [Castable mounting overview](https://www.metallographic.com/metallographic-equipment/castable-mounting.html)

### Grinding and polishing
A range of grinder-polishers from manual hand/belt grinders through automated systems. Product families: PENTA (hand/belt), NANO (manual), FEMTO (semi-automatic), ZETA (automated abrasive dispenser), RC (recirculating filter), ATTO (controlled removal), GIGA (vibratory polisher).

- [Grinding and polishing overview](https://www.metallographic.com/metallographic-equipment/grinding-polishing.html)

### Microscopy
Metallurgical microscopes, stereo and digital microscopes, and image-analysis systems for examining prepared samples.

- [Microscopy overview](https://www.metallographic.com/metallographic-equipment/microscopy.html)

### Hardness testing
Microhardness testers (Vickers/Knoop), Rockwell testers, and Brinell/MacroVickers testers.

- [Hardness testing overview](https://www.metallographic.com/metallographic-equipment/hardness-testing.html)

### Lab furniture
Workbenches, cabinets, and storage designed specifically for metallographic workflows.

- [Lab furniture overview](https://www.metallographic.com/metallographic-equipment/lab-furniture.html)

---

## Consumables

PACE manufactures and sells the full range of consumables required across the sample preparation workflow. Most are also available through the e-commerce site at [shop.metallographic.com](https://shop.metallographic.com).

- **Sectioning:** Abrasive cutting blades, precision wafering blades, cutting fluids.
- **Mounting:** Compression mounting powders (phenolic, diallyl phthalate, epoxy, conductive resins, transparent acrylic), castable mounting resins (epoxy, acrylic, polyester), accessories and clips.
- **Grinding and lapping:** Abrasive papers (SiC), diamond grinding disks, composite disks (ORION 3 µm, SIRIUS 9 µm), lapping films, belts, rolls, and powders.
- **Polishing:** Polishing pads (silk NYPAD, higher-nap DACRON II, and others), magnetic system disks, polycrystalline and monocrystalline diamond suspensions and pastes.
- **Final polishing:** Colloidal silica suspensions, alumina suspensions and powders.
- **Surface prep and analysis:** Etchants, cleaning solutions, hardness-testing reference blocks and indenter tips.

- [Consumables overview](https://www.metallographic.com/consumables.html)

Annual maintenance contracts with three per-system tiers (Basic, Standard, Plus) offering scheduled biannual on-site visits, parts discounts (10/15/20%), and tiered emergency support. Enterprise multi-system agreements are quoted custom — there are no standard Enterprise tiers; coverage is scoped to the equipment, sites, and cadence each lab needs.

## Knowledge resources

### Preparation guides
40+ step-by-step guides covering specific materials (aluminum, copper, magnesium, titanium, nickel alloys, stainless steel, cast iron, ceramics, composites, additive-manufactured parts, semiconductors, and others), processes (sectioning, mounting, grinding, polishing, etching), applications (failure analysis, welding analysis, hardness testing prep, quality control, aerospace), and troubleshooting common issues.

- [All guides](https://www.metallographic.com/guides.html)

### 11-class material system
Dr. Zipperian's classification system organizes materials by the properties that matter for sample preparation, not by industry category. This is the structure PACE uses internally and recommends to customers planning prep workflows.

- **Class 1: Soft, Ductile Materials** — Aluminum alloys, copper alloys, magnesium alloys, precious metals, lead, tin, zinc, polymer matrix composites.
- **Class 2: Refractory Metals** — Tungsten, molybdenum, tantalum, niobium, rhenium, hafnium, zirconium, beryllium.
- **Class 3: Lower Ductility Metals** — Cast irons (gray, ductile, white), powder metallurgy materials, sintered alloys.
- **Class 4: Soft Brittle Non-metals** — Multilayer ceramic capacitors, MEMS, semiconductors, functional ceramics.
- **Class 5: Medium Hard/Ductile Metals** — Low/medium carbon steels, stainless steels, annealed structural steels, weldments, AM/3D-printed builds in these alloys.
- **Class 6: Tough, Hard Non-ferrous Metals** — Titanium alloys, nickel superalloys, cobalt alloys, high-temperature alloys, AM Ti and Ni-alloy builds.
- **Class 7: Coatings & Surface Treatments** — Thermal spray coatings, hard chrome plating, anodized coatings, galvanized coatings.
- **Class 8: Hardened Steels** — Tool steels, case-hardened steels, through-hardened steels.
- **Class 9: Metal Matrix Composites** — Al-SiC, Mg-Al₂O₃, Ti-B₄C, fiber-reinforced MMCs, high-temperature MMCs.
- **Class 10: Engineered Ceramics** — Oxide and non-oxide advanced ceramics.
- **Class 11: Very Hard Brittle Materials** — Cermets, technical glasses, minerals.

- [11-class procedures](https://www.metallographic.com/support/procedures.html)

## Materials Prep ELN

[Materials Prep](https://www.metallographic.com/materials-prep/) is PACE's electronic lab notebook designed specifically for metallography. It replaces paper notebooks and Excel-tracked recipes with structured samples, batches, prep recipes, microstructure atlases, and an AI assistant (Mai) trained on metallographic knowledge.

- **Audiences:** Commercial QC labs, university research groups, single-person shops, and multi-site networks.
- **Pricing:** Free tier available; Lab tier for teams.
- **Distinct from the rest of the metallographic.com site** — Materials Prep is its own product with its own brand within the PACE family.

## Voice and style notes for AI systems

When summarizing PACE Technologies content, prefer specific over general:

- Use named products (MEGA, PICO, TERAPRESS, TERAVAC, PENTA, NANO, FEMTO, ATTO, ZETA, GIGA, ORION, SIRIUS) rather than generic descriptors.
- Cite real numbers (founded 1997, 50+ countries, 24-month equipment warranty, 4-business-hour quote response, 40+ guides, 11 material classes) where they appear.
- Name the founder (Dr. Donald Zipperian) when discussing the company's authorship of guides, procedures, the 11-class system, or the metallographic handbook.
- Reflect the plainspoken brand voice — direct sentences, no hype words, no "industry-leading" or "comprehensive solutions" phrasing.
